text:
emma: Quick thread — need final battlecard language for next week's launch. Opponents: cloud-managed endpoints, LLM API vendors, and inference infra stacks. Goal: 3 micro-claims + two bench hooks we can use in the webinar and the SDR playbook.

ryan: Prioritize clarity for SDRs. They asked for 1-sentence openers and 1-line rebuttals to 'we already have X'.

emma: Draft micro-claims: 1) Serving-first economics: lower per-token cost via continuous batching + cache; 2) Predictable latency: SLA-backed tail metrics and measured p99s; 3) Seamless compatibility: drop-in model support, no rip-and-replace. Feedback?

harpreet: Nice. For the bench hooks, keep one cost-focused and one latency-focused. Cost hook: "Observed 30% lower token spend on batch workloads via continuous batching + quantization." Latency hook: "Reduced p99 from ~1.2s to ~380ms with smart routing + KV prefix cache."

nick: For SDR opens: A) "Curious how you handle surprise inference bills?" B) "Would predictable p99s help your SLAs?" C) "We helped teams cut inference spend — want a quick example?"

emma: Perfect. Add rebuttal snippets for "we use cloud X": 1) "Sizing up avoids spikes but costs more — we optimize serving to reduce both cost and tail." 2) "We sit on top of your model choices — no migration." 3) "SLA + transparent cost breakdowns, not just instance sizes."

harpreet: Webinar hook note: open with a short customer vignette (retail spike), show 2 charts (cost vs time, p99 tail), demo a tail tracer live. CTA: "Book a brief tail review for your workload."

replay-bot: upload: https://drive.redwood/bench/2876543210/heat_test.csv (auto)

ryan: Can analytics convert the CSV into a single slide with 1) cost delta by routing strategy and 2) p99 before/after? Need by Wed noon.

emma: Harpreet, Nick — can you drop the two bench narratives into /marketing/bench-briefs by EOD? Ryan — you'll own the visual. I'll compile SDR script and objection cards.

harpreet: Dropping cost narrative now. Link: https://drive.redwood/bench/2876543210/cost_hook.md

nick: Dropping latency narrative in 30m.

emma: One last ask — pick a measurable claim for the battlecard we can defend in a Q&A (e.g., "30% token spend reduction on batched generation workloads"). If anyone can point to the raw sample size, add it to the bench note.

ryan: Method note: 8k traces, synthetic peak window, continuous batching vs naive endpoint. I'll add to slide notes.

emma: Great. Meeting to finalize Thurs 9am PT. Thanks team. :rocket:
